ai.description: This small frog reaches 25 mm. It is brownish-grey with a pale belly and lacks vomerine teeth. Distinctive features include a pointed snout and granular skin on the back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Philautus dubius* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-colored lateral bands that extend from the snout through the eye to the flanks, contrasting with its pale belly.
ai.habitat: *Philautus dubius* inhabits moist, high-altitude evergreen forests and tea plantations in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Darjeeling bubble-nest frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation of its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Philautus dubius* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in moist terrestrial habitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Philautus dubius* is endemic to the Darjeeling Himalayas in West Bengal, India, where it inhabits high-elevation forests at approximately 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Darjeeling Bubble-nest Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "tink" or "click" notes, typically heard from vegetation near water sources in montane forests.
